name: Scourwind
description: Scourwind earns its name through relentless atmospheric violence, perpetual dust storms racing across the surface at speeds that sandblast exposed equipment within hours. The thin atmosphere somehow generates wind velocities that shouldn't be possible, thermal differentials between sun-facing and shadow regions creating circulation patterns that never stabilize. The dust seas that cover the lowlands are in constant motion, their surfaces rippling with waves that can bury vehicles in minutes.

The erosion patterns carved into every exposed surface tell the story of geological ages spent under bombardment, rock sculpted into flowing shapes that seem almost organic. The rift valleys offer some shelter from the worst winds, their depths creating calmer microclimates where dust settles into deceptive smoothness. But even here, the storms find entry, funneling through gaps and canyons with amplified fury.

No civilization has left its mark on Scourwind, no ruins or artifacts suggesting anyone ever tried to establish presence here. The planet exists in a state of natural hostility that offers no resources worth the extraction cost, no strategic value worth the operational difficulty. Survey teams have visited, documented, and departed, leaving behind nothing that the wind hasn't already claimed.

Yet Scourwind attracts a certain type of visitor—those seeking solitude absolute enough to strip away all distraction, those testing equipment against worst-case conditions, those who simply want to stand against something inhuman and endure. The experience is clarifying in its simplicity: survive the wind or don't. No complexity, no negotiation, no accommodation. Scourwind offers nothing and demands everything, and some find that honest in a way the complicated universe rarely provides.
